overview: Moche societies flourished along Peru's northern coastal valleys during the first through eighth centuries CE. Their ceramics preserve an unusually rich visual record of people, animals, plants and ritual activity.

items.text: Potters used molds to produce standardized vessel shapes while varying their painted and sculpted decoration.
Many vessels combine red and cream slip painting with modeled figures. Complex scenes could cover the surface of a stirrup-spout bottle.
Portrait bottles may depict recognizable individuals. Scholars debate how their social identities related to the vessels' eventual placement in burials.
Fine decorated pottery also occurs in residential compounds. Wear, repairs and excavated household contexts show that many vessels served the living before burial.
Decorated vessels participated in household rituals and feasts, including the sharing of food and corn beer.
Images include crops, animals, healers and supernatural beings. They are a visual source, but an image alone cannot tell us every detail of the activity it depicts.

sources.title: The Met: Portrait Head Bottle, object 64.228.21
